fatal_errors: The proposed Ti-6Al-4V alloy is unrelated to the target ball-milled MgAlTiVFeCo BCC alloy processed by spark plasma sintering.
The baseline is self-contradictory: Ti-6Al-4V is called the pure-titanium baseline while also being the proposed alloy composition.
The claimed 10% density reduction is physically inconsistent with typical pure titanium and Ti-6Al-4V densities.
No evidence supports the quantitative strength-to-weight improvement or the asserted precipitation-hardening mechanism.
explanation: The hypothesis addresses lightweight structural performance only at a broad level. It misses the MgAlTiVFeCo composition, SPS treatment at 800–1000 °C, oxide barrier phases, densification and hardness results, and the oxidation and chloride-corrosion mechanisms and measurements. Tensile and density testing could falsify its own claims, but it would not discriminate the target hypothesis concerning temperature-dependent SPS consolidation, parabolic oxidation, or electrochemical corrosion resistance. Internal baseline confusion and unsupported quantitative predictions prevent it from qualifying as a well-supported plausible alternative.
